text: Ancient Indian texts called the Upanishads, dating to around 3000 BC, already discussed cloud formation, rain, and the seasonal cycle caused by Earth's movement around the Sun.
keywords: ancient india, upanishads, early meteorology, clouds

text: Around 600 BC, the Greek philosopher Thales is credited with issuing the first seasonal crop forecast, making him one of the earliest candidates for the title of first meteorologist.
keywords: thales, ancient greece, forecast, crop prediction

text: Around 350 BC, Aristotle wrote Meteorology, the first known work to systematically cover earth sciences including weather and climate. The term itself comes from the Greek meteoros, meaning 'high in the sky.'
keywords: aristotle, ancient greece, meteorology origin, etymology

text: Aristotle's student Theophrastus followed up with The Book of Signs, describing how halos around the sun or moon could be used to forecast weather. These ideas remained influential for nearly 2,000 years.
keywords: theophrastus, weather forecasting, halos, ancient greece

text: In the 1st century AD, Han dynasty philosopher Wang Chong argued against the myth that rain fell directly from the heavens, correctly proposing that water evaporates upward, forms clouds, and condenses back into rain.
keywords: wang chong, ancient china, water cycle, evaporation

text: Chinese scientist Shen Kuo described vivid accounts of tornadoes and explained rainbows as sunlight interacting with rain in his 1088 work, the Dream Pool Essays.
keywords: shen kuo, ancient china, tornado, rainbow explanation

text: In 1441, Prince Munjong of Korea's Joseon Dynasty invented the first standardized rain gauge, which was distributed across the kingdom as an official tool for assessing farmers' harvests for land taxes.
keywords: korea, joseon dynasty, rain gauge, invention

text: Around 1450, Leone Battista Alberti built a swinging-plate anemometer, generally credited as the first instrument built specifically to measure wind speed.
keywords: alberti, anemometer, wind speed, invention

text: In 1607, Galileo Galilei built a thermoscope, an early precursor to the thermometer that marked one of the first attempts to measure temperature rather than treat heat as a quality of the classical elements.
keywords: galileo, thermoscope, temperature measurement, invention

text: In 1643, Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer, a device still fundamental to measuring atmospheric pressure today.
keywords: torricelli, barometer, atmospheric pressure, invention

text: In 1654, Ferdinando II de Medici sponsored the first weather observation network, linking stations across cities including Florence, Paris, and Warsaw so that readings could be compared centrally.
keywords: medici, weather network, observation stations, italy

text: Edmund Halley, better known for his comet, published a systematic study of trade winds and monsoons in 1686, correctly identifying solar heating as the driver of atmospheric circulation.
keywords: edmund halley, trade winds, monsoon, atmospheric circulation

text: In 1724, Gabriel Fahrenheit devised a reliable mercury thermometer scale, which still bears his name and remains in everyday use in the United States.
keywords: fahrenheit, thermometer, temperature scale, invention

text: In 1742, Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius proposed the temperature scale that would eventually become the Celsius scale used across most of the world today.
keywords: celsius, temperature scale, sweden, invention

text: Benjamin Franklin, annoyed that a hurricane blocked his view of a 1743 lunar eclipse, worked out that cyclones move in the opposite direction to the winds circling their edge.
keywords: benjamin franklin, hurricane, cyclone motion, discovery

text: In 1802, British chemist Luke Howard introduced Latin names for cloud types, including cirrus, cumulus, stratus, and nimbus, a classification system that still forms the basis of cloud naming today.
keywords: luke howard, cloud classification, cirrus, cumulus, stratus

text: Francis Beaufort introduced his wind force classification system in 1806, which evolved into the Beaufort Scale still referenced in marine and meteorological forecasts today.
keywords: beaufort scale, wind classification, invention

text: In 1849, the Smithsonian Institution began building a network of about 150 weather observers across the United States who reported conditions by telegraph, an early form of real-time weather reporting.
keywords: smithsonian institution, telegraph, weather network, united states

text: The UK Meteorological Office, founded in 1854, became the world's first national meteorological service.
keywords: uk met office, national weather service, history

text: On July 31, 1861, the UK Met Office issued the first public weather forecast, an event widely regarded as the birth of modern forecasting.
keywords: first public forecast, uk met office, 1861

text: In 1904, Norwegian meteorologist Vilhelm Bjerknes proposed that the atmosphere's future state could, in principle, be calculated from physical equations of motion, an idea that underlies today's computer weather models.
keywords: vilhelm bjerknes, numerical weather prediction, equations of motion

text: Vice-Admiral Robert FitzRoy, captain of Charles Darwin's ship HMS Beagle, coined the word 'forecast' in the 1850s while pioneering some of the earliest public weather predictions.
keywords: robert fitzroy, forecast etymology, hms beagle

text: Lightning strikes the Earth roughly 40 million times a year, which works out to about 76 strikes every single minute.
keywords: lightning, frequency, statistics

text: A lightning bolt briefly reaches temperatures of around 30,000 degrees Celsius, several times hotter than the surface of the sun.
keywords: lightning, temperature, sun comparison

text: Thunder is the sound of a shockwave: air along a lightning channel is heated so quickly that it expands explosively, creating a pressure wave that reaches our ears as a rumble.
keywords: thunder, lightning, shockwave, sound

text: Clouds are not made of gas. They are a mixture of dry air, tiny liquid water droplets, and ice particles suspended in the atmosphere.
keywords: clouds, composition, water droplets, ice

text: A single snowflake can be built from up to 200 individual ice crystals, all arranged symmetrically around one tiny speck of dust.
keywords: snowflake, ice crystals, structure

text: The landscape of a region directly shapes its weather. A flat island and a nearby mountainous island can have noticeably different climates even at similar latitudes.
keywords: landscape, climate, geography, weather patterns

text: A weather 'front' is the boundary between two air masses with different temperature and moisture. Sudden weather changes usually happen when one air mass pushes the other out along this boundary.
keywords: front, air mass, weather change

text: Air temperature over land can swing by several degrees within just a few hours, but temperature over open ocean water can take weeks to shift by the same amount.
keywords: temperature change, land vs ocean, thermal inertia

text: High, wispy cirrus clouds can be an early warning sign, often forecasting a change in weather 12 to 24 hours before it actually arrives.
keywords: cirrus clouds, forecasting, early warning sign

text: In Papua New Guinea, extremely humid weather that suddenly turns into a rainstorm as the sun heats the air is known locally as 'chay nat,' which literally translates to 'rain sun.'
keywords: papua new guinea, humidity, local terminology, rainstorm

text: A waterspout is essentially a tornado that forms over a body of water rather than over land.
keywords: waterspout, tornado, water

text: The United States experiences more tornadoes than anywhere else on Earth, with more than 1,200 recorded in a typical year.
keywords: tornado, united states, frequency

text: El Nino describes a shift in Pacific Ocean currents that redistributes heat between South America and Australia, triggering major climate swings across both regions.
keywords: el nino, ocean currents, climate pattern

text: A heat wave usually forms when a high-pressure system settles over a region and stays there for an extended period, trapping warm air close to the ground.
keywords: heat wave, high pressure system, causes

text: Lake-effect snowstorms form when cold air passes over the relatively warmer waters of the Great Lakes, picking up moisture that falls as heavy snow downwind.
keywords: lake effect snow, great lakes, snowstorm

text: A 'Nor'easter' is a storm system with cold air at its core that forms over non-tropical regions, commonly affecting North America's northeastern coast.
keywords: nor'easter, storm system, north america

text: The main difference between a tropical storm and a hurricane is wind speed. Once a storm's sustained winds cross a set threshold, it gets reclassified as a hurricane.
keywords: tropical storm, hurricane, classification, wind speed

text: Roughly one-third of all weather-related deaths worldwide are caused by tropical cyclones.
keywords: tropical cyclone, mortality, statistics

text: Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo is often called the lightning capital of the world, with visible lightning on roughly 300 nights a year, yet thunder is rarely heard because the storms form so high overhead.
keywords: lake maracaibo, venezuela, lightning capital

text: The officially recognized highest temperature on Earth is 56.7 degrees Celsius (134.1 F), recorded at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California, on July 10, 1913, though many modern meteorologists dispute the reading's accuracy.
keywords: highest temperature, death valley, furnace creek, world record

text: The coldest temperature ever directly measured at the surface is minus 89.2 degrees Celsius (-128.6 F), recorded at Vostok Station, Antarctica, on July 21, 1983.
keywords: coldest temperature, antarctica, vostok station, world record

text: Satellite data suggests an even colder spot in Antarctica may have reached around minus 93.2 degrees Celsius (-135.8 F) in 2010, though this reading is not counted as an official surface air-temperature record.
keywords: antarctica, satellite measurement, extreme cold, unofficial record

text: The wettest inhabited place on Earth is Mawsynram, India, which receives an average of about 467 inches (11,861 mm) of rainfall every year.
keywords: wettest place, mawsynram, india, rainfall record

text: The McMurdo Dry Valleys in Antarctica are considered the driest place on Earth, with an average annual precipitation of just 0.07 inches (about 2 mm).
keywords: driest place, mcmurdo dry valleys, antarctica, precipitation record

text: The longest single lightning bolt ever measured stretched 767.6 km (477.8 miles) across parts of the southern United States in 2020, roughly the driving distance between New York City and Columbus, Ohio.
keywords: longest lightning bolt, world record, 2020

text: The world's largest recorded hailstone fell in Vivian, South Dakota, in 2010, measuring 7.99 inches wide and weighing 1.9 pounds.
keywords: largest hailstone, south dakota, world record

text: The highest dew point ever recorded was 35 degrees Celsius (95 F) at Dhahran, Saudi Arabia, in 2003, while the air temperature that day sat at 42 C (108 F), pushing the heat index to a scorching 81.1 C (178 F).
keywords: highest dew point, dhahran, saudi arabia, heat index

text: Canada's national temperature record was set in 2021 at Lytton, British Columbia, which reached 49.6 degrees Celsius (121.3 F) during a historic heat dome, just days before the town was destroyed by wildfire.
keywords: canada, lytton, heat dome, national record

text: Death Valley holds the record for the highest average monthly temperature ever recorded anywhere on Earth, at 42.5 degrees Celsius (108.5 F).
keywords: death valley, average monthly temperature, world record

text: Death Valley also holds the record for the most consecutive days above 48.9 degrees Celsius (120 F), a stretch of 40 straight days of extreme heat.
keywords: death valley, heat streak, consecutive days, world record

text: Marble Bar, Western Australia, holds the record for the longest heat streak above 37.8 degrees Celsius (100 F): 160 consecutive days.
keywords: marble bar, australia, heat streak, world record

text: Kuwait's Mitribah weather station once recorded 20 days within a single month with temperatures at or above 50 degrees Celsius (122 F).
keywords: kuwait, mitribah, extreme heat, monthly record

text: The city of Verkhoyansk, Russia, recorded a temperature of 38 degrees Celsius (100.4 F) in 2020, a remarkable reading given that it sits north of the Arctic Circle.
keywords: verkhoyansk, russia, arctic circle, extreme heat

text: The hottest single day for the entire planet on record was July 22, 2024, when the global average temperature reached 17.16 degrees Celsius (62.89 F), narrowly beating the record set just one day earlier.
keywords: global average temperature, hottest day, 2024, climate record

text: Hurricane Katrina in 2005, one of the costliest and deadliest hurricanes on record, caused roughly 10,000 deaths and reshaped US disaster preparedness policy.
keywords: hurricane katrina, 2005, deadliest hurricane

text: According to a World Economic Forum report, natural disasters, many of them weather-related, have increased roughly five-fold in frequency over the past five decades.
keywords: natural disasters, world economic forum, statistics, trend

text: Despite natural disasters becoming more frequent, better forecasting and disaster management have cut weather-related death tolls to about a third of what they were fifty years ago.
keywords: disaster management, mortality trend, forecasting improvement

text: Over the past 50 years, extreme weather events are estimated to have cost the United States more than 3.6 trillion dollars.
keywords: united states, economic cost, extreme weather, statistics

text: A 1977 drought remains the costliest single weather event in Canadian history.
keywords: canada, drought, 1977, economic cost

text: Around 89 percent of Africa's weather-related deaths over the past 50 years have come from just four major droughts.
keywords: africa, drought, mortality, statistics

text: The US National Weather Service has been keeping systematic weather records across the United States since 1870.
keywords: national weather service, record keeping, history, united states

text: Modern satellites are responsible for roughly three-quarters of the accuracy improvements seen in weather forecasting over the past several decades.
keywords: satellites, forecast accuracy, technology impact

text: The US National Weather Service operates 159 radar towers, giving it near-complete Doppler radar coverage of the continental United States.
keywords: doppler radar, national weather service, coverage, technology

text: Antarctica's warmest recorded temperature is a comparatively mild 19.8 degrees Celsius (67.6 F), recorded at Signy Research Station on Signy Island, a striking contrast to the continent's brutal winter lows.
keywords: antarctica, warmest recorded temperature, signy research station

text: The highest temperature ever recorded alongside 100 percent relative humidity was 34 degrees Celsius (93 F), observed in Jask, Iran, in 2012, meaning the air was fully saturated with moisture while still dangerously hot.
keywords: jask iran, relative humidity, extreme heat, world record

text: Old sailors' lore holds that unusually clear air, where distant objects appear sharper than normal, is itself a sign that rain is on its way.
keywords: weather proverb, clear air, rain sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: The saying 'red sky at night, sailor's delight; red sky at morning, sailor take warning' ties a red sunset to fair weather moving in, and a red sunrise to a storm approaching from the west.
keywords: red sky, weather proverb, sailors
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: A related rhyme puts it this way: an evening sky tinted red and a morning sky tinted gray promise a fine day, but the reverse combination means you had better grab a hat before you get soaked.
keywords: weather proverb, evening red, morning gray
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: 'If it rains before seven, it will clear before eleven' reflects how fast-moving morning weather systems often clear up by midday.
keywords: weather proverb, morning rain, clearing weather
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: The old rhyme 'rain from the south prevents the drought, but rain from the west is always best' is tied to regional wind and storm-track patterns.
keywords: weather proverb, wind direction, rain source
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: Folklore warns that anvil-shaped clouds, the flattened tops of towering thunderstorms, are a sign that a gale is on its way.
keywords: weather proverb, anvil clouds, gale warning
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: According to old weather sayings, a cloud with a rounded top and a flat base is likely to bring rain.
keywords: weather proverb, cloud shape, rain sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: When small clouds start joining together and thickening, traditional lore says rain is on the way.
keywords: weather proverb, clouds thickening, rain sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: Black clouds appearing in the north during winter were traditionally read as a sign that snow was approaching.
keywords: weather proverb, black clouds, winter, snow sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: An old saying claims that once there is enough blue sky to 'patch a Dutchman's breeches,' the weather is about to clear.
keywords: weather proverb, blue sky, clearing weather
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: A 'curdly,' mottled sky was said in old farming lore to mean the ground would not stay dry for long.
keywords: weather proverb, curdly sky, rain sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: If clouds appear to drift against the direction of the surface wind, folklore says a storm is brewing.
keywords: weather proverb, clouds crosswind, storm sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: The old rhyme 'hen scarts and filly tails make lofty ships wear low sails' uses fanciful cloud-shape names to warn sailors of rough weather ahead.
keywords: weather proverb, hen scarts, filly tails, sailors
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: Clouds that hang low enough to cast visible shadows on the ground are traditionally seen as a sign that rain will soon follow.
keywords: weather proverb, low clouds, shadows, rain sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: 'Mackerel sky, mackerel sky, never long wet, never long dry' describes rippled, scale-like clouds said to predict a short-lived change in weather.
keywords: weather proverb, mackerel sky, cloud pattern
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: 'If three nights dewless there be, twill rain, you're sure to see' links a stretch of mornings without dew to an approaching rain spell.
keywords: weather proverb, dew, rain sign
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: Folklore holds that if morning dew dries quickly, fair weather is likely, but if it lingers on the grass, rain may follow within a day.
keywords: weather proverb, dew drying, rain prediction
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: 'With dew before midnight, the next day sure will be bright' ties early dew formation to a clear, sunny day ahead.
keywords: weather proverb, dew before midnight, clear day
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)

text: According to old lore, if your feet get wet from morning dew, you can expect to stay dry for the rest of the day.
keywords: weather proverb, wet feet, dew, dry day
source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Weather Proverbs and Prognostics (paraphrased)
